In law , a question of law , also known as a point of law , is a question that must be answered by a judge and can not be answered by a jury. [ 1 ] Such a question is distinct from a question of fact , which must be answered by reference to facts and evidence as well as inferences arising from those facts. Answers to questions of law are generally expressed in terms of broad legal principles. They can be applied to many situations rather than particular circumstances or facts. An answer to a question of law as applied to the specific facts of a case is often referred to as a conclusion of law .
